# Architecture

* [The construction model](construction-model.md) - How a design records what is cut and how it is sewn: materials with synchronised looks, overlay pieces on their own layer, finishes with real widths, curvature-continuous lines, paired pieces, and what the pattern export reads from them.
* [Editor architecture for the designer tool](editor-architecture.md) (draft) - Module layout and core algorithms for turning the POC into the designer tool: command-driven document, projected surface splines, explicit curve insertion into the canonical mesh, per-panel flattening for cloth-space UVs, swept rims and straps, generator-driven stones, and the frame budget.
* [Genesis 9 as the canonical mesh (feasibility)](genesis9-as-canonical-mesh.md) (draft) - Feasibility of replacing the MakeHuman mannequin (41,595 vertices) with Daz Genesis 9 subdivided once (99,688 vertices) as the canonical topology every design is anchored to: exactly symmetric, one piece, all quads, 116 joint correctives; removes the wrap; costs a one-time migration, ~2.4x triangles and a hard dependency on Daz Interactive Licenses. Recommendation: switch, after a performance spike.
* [POC-to-product gap - the garment must become data](poc-to-product-gap.md) (draft) - What the three.js POC can be reused for and what must change: the garment's shape is hard-coded as analytic fields, and the professional tool needs it as an editable, serialisable panel model that flattens to patterns.
* [Procedural stone patterns](procedural-stone-patterns.md) (draft) - A stone group as a live procedure on the flat cloth of one piece: an arrangement (48, offered as about 150 presets) with its own sizing, a frame that moves the whole of it, a stack of modifiers on density, size and colour, distortions, handles over the view specific to each kind; what the design hangs on is placed first, and everything re-runs within a frame of a drag.

# Data Model

* [Design document model (garment as data)](design-document-model.md) (draft) - The serialisable design file every tool edits: body and pose, a curve graph on the canonical body, panels derived from it with fabric stacks, straps, trims, decals and procedural stone generators; all edits are commands, everything derived is a rebuildable cache.

# Design Note

* [The Mirror toggle and paired parts](mirror-toggle.md) (draft) - One toolbar toggle decides whether an edit reaches both sides of the body. Mirror off, an edit of a paired part splits the pair permanently; there is no per-part mirror control.
